open_obligations: Check whether the DPO training runs show any of the honest-then-lying cycling Irving et al. describe, or whether too few iterations were run to observe it.
Confirm that judge accuracy, not only debater win rate, was tracked across all checkpoints.
Note the judge is never trained on the debaters' transcripts, and check how it compares with the judge in Irving et al.'s proposal.
in.other_title: Stronger trained debaters yield +4 points judge accuracy; no effect for consultants
in.rationale: Irving et al. ask whether self-play stably converges to honest debate equilibria and know of no theory guaranteeing it. Arnesen et al. report that self-play DPO training of their debaters is associated with 4 percentage points higher judge accuracy for the fully DPO-trained model than for the SFT model (p < 10^-6); this is empirical evidence comparing the fully DPO-trained and SFT debaters with a judge never trained on their transcripts, not a convergence result.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether self-play training of debaters moves toward truth-favouring outcomes rather than unstable cycles, for DPO-trained debater models

open_obligations: Check whether the paper proves convergence of any training procedure or only correctness at (approximate) Stackelberg equilibria.
Verify that the Stackelberg setting (one debater leads) matches the simultaneous self-play Irving et al. had in mind.
Check that rho-stability and A-provability are plausible for the questions of interest.
in.other_title: Theorem 6.2: correct answers at Stackelberg equilibria (prob. 1 - 5 eps)
in.rationale: Irving et al. note no theory says self-play stably converges to optimal play. Brown-Cohen et al. state that prover-estimator debaters can be trained with standard methods that converge to Stackelberg equilibria, and Theorem 6.2 gives correct answers with probability at least 1 - 5 eps at A-leading Stackelberg equilibria under rho-stability and A-provability; this characterises equilibria rather than proving that gradient training converges.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether standard training can be expected to reach debate equilibria that give correct answers, in complexity-theoretic recursive debate with stable decompositions

text: The authors ask whether debate's Nash equilibria can be found by some version of gradient descent, noting they know of no theory saying self-play should stably converge to optimal play. They describe a possible bad cycle in which both agents become honest, forget how to point out lies, and then one agent returns to lying and wins for a while.
title: Does self-play training stably converge to honest debate equilibria?
